items.title: La patronal maderera contradice a Moreno sobre el incendio de Niebla: “El culpable no es el eucalipto, sino la clase política”
items.description: La patronal de empresas madereras de Huelva ha achacado este miércoles la virulencia del reciente incendio de Niebla (Huelva) a “la falta de gestión pública y a la desidia política hacia las masas forestales”, lo que contradice las explicaciones del presidente andaluz, Juan Manuel Moreno (PP), que responsabilizó al eucalipto de la velocidad del fuego, que tardó 10 días en ser controlado. Las compañías onubenses han cargado con dureza contra el Gobierno andaluz, al que culpan de tener montes públicos sin dedicarles un mínimo de conservación, lo que ha acumulado una biomasa que ayudó a la rápida expansión de las llamas hasta calcinar 33.000 hectáreas de montes. items.title: Ogou : Mise en œuvre du projet « Tamarin » : Les acteurs des Plateaux consultés
items.description: Atakpamé, 26 août (ATOP) – Un atelier régional de consultation consacré au lancement du projet « Tamarin Clean Cooking » s’est tenu le mercredi 26 août à Atakpamé. Portée par l’entreprise togolaise Tamarin Clean Cooking avec le soutien de S2 Services et hummingbirds, cette initiative vise à distribuer plus de 150 000 foyers améliorés à travers quatre régions du pays notamment Kara, Centrale, Plateaux et Maritime. L’objectif est de lutter contre la déforestation et réduire les émissions de gaz à effet de serre. Les échanges ont essentiellement porté sur l’urgence de passer de l’observation à l’action pour faire face à la dégradation progressive du couvert végétal et à l’impact sanitaire des foyers traditionnels, le basculement vers l’utilisation massive des foyers améliorés qui est une priorité d’action publique. Les participants ont suivi une présentation du mécanisme de la finance carbone et de la compensation internationale et sur l’importance de la consultation des parties prenantes. Ils ont aussi débattu du rôle des femmes reconnues comme actrices principales et premières bénéficiaires de cette transition énergétique, tant pour leur santé que pour leur autonomisation socio-économique. Le gouverneur de la région des Plateaux, Général de brigade Dadja Maganawé, a souligné l’urgence environnementale et sanitaire qui pèse sur les populations locales. « Derrière le mode de cuisson se trouvent des enjeux qui touchent directement notre environnement, la santé de nos familles et la qualité de vie de nos communautés. Chaque arbre abattu sans mesure alternative altère le visage de notre région. Chaque foyer traditionnel qui fume dans nos concessions compromet la santé de nos familles. Face à ce constat, nous ne sommes plus à l’heure de simples observations, nous sommes à l’heure des choix et de l’action », a-t-il indiqué. Le chef projet, Ndongbok Durando a rappelé la dimension à la fois économique, environnementale et sociale du programme. « Notre foyer peut réduire la consommation de bois de plus de 60 % et le temps pour les collecter. Il réduit les flammes, la fumée, le temps de cuisson. C’est une contribution certes petite, mais très importante, car nous allons chercher les ménages les plus éloignés qui utilisent le foyer à trois pierres », a-t-il souligné. M. Ndongbok a fait savoir que grâce au mécanisme de la finance climatique et à la certification Gold Standard, la valorisation des réductions d’émissions sous forme de crédits carbone permettra de subsidier le coût de ces équipements, garantissant ainsi un accès universel à une énergie de cuisson propre, sûre et abordable pour les ménages. ATOP/AY/KKT/BA

items.title: Des blindés de pointe couverts de toiles d'araignée dans les forêts : les médias révèlent le triste sort des chars occidentaux en Ukraine
items.description: Presque des le debut de l'operation militaire speciale en Ukraine, en fevrier 2022, Kiev a demande a plusieurs reprises de lui fournir des chars de type occidental. Aujourd'hui, plusieurs annees plus tard, ces engins de combat d'une valeur de 10 millions de dollars, autrefois indispensables a l'armee ukrainienne, sont pour la plupart a l'abandon, recouverts de toiles d'araignee, dans les forets : ils se sont reveles impuissants sur le champ de bataille face a des drones bon marche, a rapporte le 25 août le New York Times (NYT), citant des militaires ukrainiens. Le journal americain a rappele que, malgre les nombreuses demandes de Kiev, les allies occidentaux s'etaient abstenus de les livrer jusqu'en janvier 2023, date a laquelle le Royaume-Uni, l'Allemagne et les etats-Unis ont revu leur position. Une brigade speciale a ete creee au sein de l'armee ukrainienne, formee notamment pour utiliser ces blindes occidentaux. Cependant, au moment ou elle est entree au combat a la fin du printemps 2023, les drones bon marche avaient deja commence a toucher ces engins, a note le New York Times . a la meme epoque, a rappele le journal, les forces armees russes ont commence a equiper leurs chars de filets et de grilles anti-drones. Comme l'ont admis des soldats ukrainiens lors d'un entretien avec le NYT , la Russie allait dans la bonne direction. Des vehicules blindes occidentaux de pointe utilises comme tracteurs D'apres le journal americain, les chars occidentaux sont toujours en service au sein de l'armee ukrainienne, et les soldats effectuent des exercices de tir environ une fois toutes les deux semaines. Cependant, ces engins de combat se trouvent loin a l'arriere, dissimules sous des filets de camouflage : certains attendent d'etre repares ou entretenus, d'autres font partie de la reserve operationnelle. Selon les declarations d'un des interlocuteurs du NYT , l'un des chars a roule sur une mine et a pris feu, tandis qu'un autre a ete touche par un drone. Ces dommages n'ont meme pas ete subis au cours des combats, mais lors d'une « evacuation », alors que les chars etaient utilises comme des tracteurs coûteux pour remorquer du materiel. Depuis le debut des livraisons de blindes occidentaux et leur mise en service au sein de l'armee ukrainienne, le ministere russe de la Defense a signale a plusieurs reprises leur capture ou leur destruction sur le champ de bataille. Le 7 juin 2023, le regime de Kiev a perdu , lors d'une seule attaque, des dizaines de chars et de vehicules de combat occidentaux. Certains engins, parmi lesquels des Leopard 2 allemands et des Abrams americains, ont ete exposes a Moscou en tant que trophees. Le Kremlin a deja declare qu'aucune des armes que l'Ukraine pourrait recevoir a l'avenir n'aurait d'influence decisive sur le deroulement des operations militaires. Moscou a egalement condamne a plusieurs reprises les livraisons d'aide militaire a l'Ukraine, affirmant que cela ne faisait que prolonger le conflit.

items.title: What Are Jewish Voters Supposed to Do?
items.description: Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube On this week’s episode of The David Frum Show , The Atlantic ’s David Frum opens with his thoughts on the blowing up of trade talks between the United States and Canada, and President Trump’s reckless trade war against Canada. David discusses how this trade war hurts not only America’s relationship with Canada but its global standing as a reliable trade partner. Then David is joined by Michigan Attorney General Dana Nessel to discuss the growing hostility among some Democratic voters toward American Jews. Frum and Nessel discuss why the rhetoric of Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed concerns some Jews; rise of anti-Semitism within the Democratic party; and the impossible situation many Jewish voters find themselves in today. Finally, David ends the show with his thoughts on the new biography on Roy Cohn, American Scoundrel . The following is a transcript of the episode: Dana Nessel: I think it’s a fundamental mistake for the Democratic Party to think that you can just push Jewish Democrats out and simply replace them with any other population. [ Music ] David Frum: Welcome to The David Frum Show. I’m David Frum, a staff writer at The Atlantic. My guest this week will be Dana Nessel, attorney general of the state of Michigan, and this week’s book will be the newly released biography American Scoundrel , a biography of Roy Cohn and his lifetime from Joe McCarthy to Donald Trump. Before either the dialogue with Attorney General Nessel or the book, I want to open with some thoughts about the recent blowup in trade negotiations between the United States and Canada. Now, it’s the Trump administration, though, so those negotiations are blown up as I record on Monday, August 24th. They may be back on by the time you watch on Wednesday, August 26th. Anything can happen with this crazy crew. But let’s assume, as I record, that the negotiations remain blown up for some time. Now, I wrote in The Atlantic this past weekend an analysis of the economic effect of the blowup of these negotiations, and I hope you’ll take a look at that. Facts, figures, dates, numbers. What I want to talk about today is not the economics—you can read that in The Atlantic, and I hope you will. What I want to talk about is some of the geopolitical implications of the United States behaving in the predatory way that the Trump administration has led the United States to behave in these negotiations with Canada. Look, I’m recording this in Canada right now as I speak. I do have a Canadian point of view. But I think I can speak more broadly when I say that America has enormously benefited all around the world in reputation and standing from its relationship with Canada. The U.S.-Canada relationship is a kind of text proof of America’s benignity and good intentions. If you’re a country anywhere in the world, wondering whether to partner with the United States or one of its adversaries—the Soviet Union in the olden days, Russia or China now—you’d look at the U.S.-Canada relationship and say, There is America’s nearest neighbor, a country only one-tenth the size of the United States—smaller in economics, smaller in population—highly vulnerable to American pressure, and yet America has consistently treated Canada as an equal, as a partner, and as a friend. And that model relationship is a proof of the good intentions of America to anybody. And so there you are on the other side of the world thinking, Can we trust the Americans? Think, Well, the Canadians next door; they trust the Americans. They’ve benefited from that trust. They’ve been treated with equality. So will we. So long as the relationship worked, America stood proud in the eyes of the world. The Trump vision of America is very different. At home, Trump’s vision of how America should arrange its economy borrows a lot from China. As much as Trump rails against China, he wants America to be more like China. His government is taking ownership stakes in major corporations. Favors are dispensed according to cronyism and patronage. He attempts to intervene in the courts on behalf of his own interests in a way that [is] very familiar to those who follow the horrible precedents of the Chinese Communist Party. And internationally, his foreign policy looks not like America as we knew it—the world leader of a coalition of democratic states bound by agreements and treaties negotiated in good faith—but like Russia, a country that has given up on the rest of the world in order to be a bully and hegemon at home. I think a lot of Canadians feel that what Trump wants from these trade negotiations is not actually any kind of deal. He wants to turn Canada into a kind of American Belarus—a satellite state, nominally independent, but in fact governed from the capital, that can be dominated to create a larger imperial zone where the imperial power does its economics not by trade and mutual benefit, but by domination, predation, and exploitation. If you’re a country on the other side of the world without a long, friendly history with the United States, if you’re an Indonesia, if you’re a Malaysia, if you’re a Philippines, if you’re a Vietnam, and you look at what Trump is doing to Canada, you think, What will they do to me? We don’t share a language with the Americans. We were not their allies in two world wars. If they will do that to their nearest neighbor and closest partner, what will they do to us? And it sends a message to the whole planet that America is reinventing itself—not as the leader of a league of democracies, but as an imperial power. Much like other imperial powers, much like Russia, much like China. Corrupt at home, dominant abroad, and maybe somebody you have to deal with because they’re so big and rich and powerful, but not someone you want to be a partner with. Certainly not someone you can trust. The message to the world from the blowup of U.S.-Canada relations is: Look, the Canadians, they’ve got the geography they’ve got. They have very few options. Ditto Mexico. But we? We’re farther away. We have options. And what would be wise for us is to keep an equal distance between the United States and China as we keep an equal distance between the United States and Russia, because what Trump is proving to us again and again is that America is no different and no better than those other powers. That’s one of Donald Trump’s big ideas. He’s said often in interviews, even when he was running for president and in his first term, Do you think we’re any different from anybody else? He really doesn’t believe America’s different from anybody else, and he’s led America to behave in ways that are no different from anybody else. But, you know, one of the things that Canadians have kept alive through all these dark months is a confidence that the Americans really are different from everybody else—and that the past of the American-Canadian relationship, that’s the truth. And it’s the present that is the dead end and the false start and the misdirection. So what we all try to keep alive here—and I speak to you from the north shore of Lake Ontario, from a road named for the losers of the American Revolution, Loyalist Parkway—the faith that is kept alive here is a faith that there’s a better America, and maybe someday it will rediscover itself. I hope that’s a faith that Americans can rediscover, too, and hold onto, too, through some very dark chapters. And now my dialogue with Attorney General Dana Nessel. [ Music ] Frum: Dana Nessel has spent the past eight years as Michigan’s attorney general. She built her career litigating civil-rights cases before winning the attorney general’s office in 2018. In office, she closed an investigation into Michigan State University’s handling of the Larry Nassar sexual-abuse scandal, led the state prosecution of the men who plotted to kidnap Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer, and brought charges against 16 Republicans who falsely certified Trump as Michigan’s 2020 election winner. Term-limited out of office this January, Nessel has become an important voice in debates over the future of the Democratic Party of Michigan, and especially against the anti-Semitism she sees rising within it. She was born in West Bloomfield Township: the site of the March 12th, 2026, terror attack on Temple Israel, the nation’s largest Reform synagogue, and a preschool with 140 children inside. Attorney General Nessel, thank you for joining me today. Nessel: Thanks for having me. Frum: Let’s start, if we may, by just talking a little bit about your personal experiences as a Jewish Democrat in Michigan. You have said that you have felt unsafe attending your own party’s state convention. Tell us what it has been like this summer for you. Nessel: Well, look, it’s been difficult, candidly, since I entered office, and it’s strange because I sort of built my career prior to becoming attorney general on being an advocate for LGBTQ rights and being very involved in the marriage-equality case that ultimately was resolved by the United States Supreme Court. And this has been my focus for much of the time. Yes, I’m also Jewish, but I’m a gay person in a same-sex marriage, and I had really thought coming into office that was what would make me stand out or be unusual as the first openly gay person to serve in statewide office in Michigan. But that’s not really been my experience, and in fact, since I’ve been in office, it’s been much more interesting to people that I’m actually the first Jewish attorney general in Michigan history. And I would say that, again, I have been bombarded with death threats since the first days that I took office. And at any given time normally, there’s about three people who are currently either serving a sentence in state or federal prison or on probation or somewhere in the proceedings for anti-Semitic death threats against me. So that was a surprise to me. But things changed in so many different ways after October 7th. And then it wasn’t just, basically, I would say mentally unstable people on the far right that were threatening me or other Jews, but now it became really a both-sides situation, and I began to perceive an enormous amount of anti-Semitism within the Democratic Party. And so it’s been a challenge since that time, and it’s gotten worse and worse. And what I am seeing from, again, people that I know in my party [is] a fundamental lack of knowledge about Judaism, about my religion, as well as about sort of the historical aspects of the state of Israel and also a complete ignorance about what ties Jews around the globe to Israel itself. And I think that’s really caused a rise in, again, they would call it anti-Zionism, but I call it anti-Semitism. Frum: Let’s talk a little bit about the reaction or the aftermath of this dreadful attack, attempted attack, on Temple Israel this year. It would’ve targeted children above all—potentially as many as 140 school-aged children. That’s your town, as I said in the introduction. What has it been like to be in a state where such a thing could happen, and how has the reaction to that terrible attempt lived up to, or not lived up to, your hopes and expectations for your state? Nessel: Well, first of all, I learned about what was happening at Temple Israel from my own son, who was at my parents’ house, that’s just down the street from Temple Israel. And so it was close enough that you could hear all the sirens and all the commotion going on. And I have many members of my family that have been longtime members of Temple Israel. It’s really a focal point of the Jewish community, because it is the biggest Reform temple anywhere in the world. But, you know, the reaction to it—obviously there’s a lot of people who were quick to call this out. But, you know, I think most concerning, of course, was the statement that our nominee for U.S. Senate made, which was that “hurt people hurt people.” And a lot of us perceived that as sort of making excuses for somebody who sought to murder over 100 pre-K schoolchildren. And that’s the kind of mentality that bothers me a lot. I will tell you that in 2019, very early on in my tenure, you had that attack in New Zealand—the Christchurch attack that killed over 50 Muslims who were in the process of their congregation and praying. And I immediately went to one of the mosques in Dearborn, and I donned a hijab to be respectful, and I talked about Islamophobia and said it was unacceptable in any realm for any reason. And I didn’t try to get into, like, what were the motivations of the person who killed these people, and did he have mental-health issues? Did he have bad experiences with Muslims? I just condemned it unequivocally, and I think that’s what people should have done with Temple Israel. You can’t make excuses for that kind of domestic terrorism. Frum: Well, since you’ve raised the Democratic nominee, let me go through the timeline of his statements, so we get a sense of what is fair to say about those statements and what is not. The attempt happened, as you say, on March the 12th of this year. It was heroically averted, and the gunman was deservedly the only casualty, or the would-be gunman. On March 12th, Abdul El-Sayed, who was not yet then the nominee, released a statement that said, “I was horrified and heartbroken this afternoon to hear the reports of an active shooter at Temple Israel in West Bloomfield. I’m thankful that no worshippers, students, or teachers were harmed. We all owe a debt of gratitude to Temple security and law enforcement, who acted swiftly to keep the community safe. To my Jewish sisters and brothers, you have a right to worship in peace … there is no room for antisemitism in America.” So that’s good. That was a statement written by who knows who. Nessel: Yeah. So I will say this. And again, I leave room for the fact that all of us have the opportunity to learn more. Frum: All right, let me ask you more about your experience. What I am most focused on is ensuring that we have safe, secure, accurate, democratic elections, which we always do, but that also those elections are certified. We have three different congressional districts that could very well swing from red to blue. And so, I know that the White House is hyperfocused on Michigan. And the fact that we have very progressive ideals that we’ve worked hard on. And whether you’re looking all the way back—to whether it’s women’s suffrage, whether it’s the fight for rights for African Americans in this country, whether it’s work that I did and many other Jews on LGBTQ-rights issues—we have been an essential part of the fabric of the Democratic Party for a very, very long time. We are an essential part of the fabric of this party, and I would ask the leadership and members of this party to consider that before they do or say things that will force us to leave this party. I feel like we’re already not wanted in the Republican Party, and I think that this is, you know, essentially a party of fascism. And we know about all the excuses that they make on the far right, and how they embrace the Nick Fuentes and Candace Owens and all the people, and Tucker Carlsons, all of the enormous anti-Semites on the far right. And I’m not a member of the Republican Party. I can only speak to being a member of the Democratic Party. But I would tell members of our party that this is a worse place without Jews in it. David Frum: Well, one of the things that people will say, and I think this is a message that Abdul El-Sayed and many of his supporters say, is: All you have to do to be accepted as a Jew is to jettison Israel. That’s all we ask. And just disavow the fate of half the Jewish people who live in the state of Israel. Maybe they’ll be massacred, maybe they’ll be enslaved. Who knows what, maybe they’ll be raped. Just separate yourself from that, and you’ll be left alone. And I think I listen to that, and I hear, first—it’s not for you to say what is important to me. When you tell me that Israel is not integral to being a Jew, you know, I don’t walk into your house and tell you what is integral to being who you are. So don’t walk into my house and tell me what is integral to being me. But second, that’s a pretty contemptible offer. You’ll guarantee my physical safety if I submit? I mean, 3,000 years of Jewish martyrdom has been people who—it’s a stubborn people, as it says in the Bible itself. We don’t submit to that. And now you’re asking us to, with a threat, maybe sometimes with a smile and a threat, but a threat. Disavow yourself, and you’ll be safe. You say, you know what? The whole point of the state of Israel was that Jews didn’t have to put their safety at the mercy of other people. They could defend themselves. And that’s the Jewish project—is to have a place in the world where Jews are safe because of themselves. And the American project was to say everyone is safe. It doesn’t matter who you are, because we don’t have majorities that tolerate minorities here. It’s not with permission from other people. It’s not conditional. Your safety is nonconditional. That’s George Washington’s famous letter to the Newport Synagogue. Your safety is nonconditional. You’re an American. You have a right to be the same as anybody else, and to be left alone and respected the same as anybody else. And now suddenly there are all kinds of conditions, but only if you disavow who you are. Nessel: Yeah. Let me just respond to that in a couple different ways. I’ve said this over and over again, that when a Black person says, That phrase that you’re using, or the way you’re talking about this issue, to me, is racist. I’d like you to stop doing it —we respect that. When we’re talking to somebody in the LGBTQ community and say, I don’t like the phrase that you’re using, or, That term is offensive to me, and here’s why— we respect that in the Democratic Party. We say, Okay, I’m not going to use that phrase anymore. I didn’t realize that it was offensive to you. I’m going to stop. But this has been an outlier for me. I have people saying, You are not going to tell us what you deem to be anti-Semitic. We’ll decide what’s anti-Semitic. That’s not up for you, the Jewish population, to decide. And I find that to be very off-putting and offensive. And I think that’s totally unacceptable. But the last thing I will say is this, if that’s the deal that has to be made—and I’ve been really candid about this—I was Jewish before I was ever Michigan attorney general. I’m going to be Jewish afterwards. I was Jewish before I was ever a member of the Democratic Party, and if I have to, I’ll be Jewish afterwards, too. Frum: Attorney General Nessel, thank you so much for joining me today on The David Frum Show. Nessel: Thanks for having me. [ Music ] Frum: Thanks so much to Dana Nessel for joining me today on The David Frum Show. As mentioned at the top of the program, my book this week is a new biography of Roy Cohn: American Scoundrel: Roy Cohn’s Dark Journey from Joe McCarthy to Donald Trump by Kai Bird and Susan Goldmark. I had the opportunity to meet the notorious Roy Cohn once in my life, when I was an undergraduate at Yale. He came to address a group of students. It was a small group, because the name of Joe McCarthy’s famous henchman had obscured a little bit with the passage of time. There were maybe six or eight of us there, and we all observed he was just as creepy in person as he was creepy in legend. And that’s the story that is told by Kai Bird and Susan Goldmark in their new book. Roy Cohn, of course, was the chief aide to Joe McCarthy during his investigations of the early 1950s. Those investigations led to disaster for McCarthy, who was eventually censured by the Senate and who died of alcoholism as a comparatively young man in 1957. But Roy Cohn went on to a more lucrative future, even if he never lost his notoriety. As a shady lawyer in New York, he handled divorces. He represented many Mafia figures. He was involved in all kinds of proceedings that would have got anybody else disbarred or even sent to prison. But Roy Cohn went from fame to fame, progress to progress. He never paid his taxes. So despite all of his amazing career success, he died broke because he owed millions of dollars to the IRS, which they reclaimed from his estate, leaving very little behind. But he certainly lived life the way he wanted to live it. Kai Bird and Susan Goldmark tell a withering story of his career, but they also illustrate how many people who thought they despised him and despised his politics were drawn into his orbit because of Roy Cohn’s fathomless ability to find favors that people wanted and to deliver them. He lived by a code of loyalty, and he drew into his network of favor-exchange many people who would become pillars of the New York liberal establishment of the 1960s and 1970s. Roy Cohn was a bad man, and he fully deserves the nickname of “American scoundrel” that he’s given in this book. But there is a blind spot in the book, and a blind spot in the way that people think about him that I kept dealing with as I read this otherwise fascinating and important book. One of the characteristics of post-McCarthy America is that, having felt so bad about the way people were accused falsely and dragged into conspiracies and had their names besmirched—some of them innocent, some of them merely naive fellow travelers. Some comparatively few of them actual traitors or spies. But there became a kind of blind spot about the moral decision to have been a communist in the 1930s and 1940s, and I noticed that throughout the biography of Roy Cohn. Kai Bird previously wrote a biography of the great scientist Robert Oppenheimer. In fact, it is his 2005 biography of Robert Oppenheimer that became the basis for the Christopher Nolan 2023 movie. Now, if you’ve seen Oppenheimer , one of the things you see is that Oppenheimer is the victim of a false persecution because of his left-wing sympathies in the 1930s, which are suggested in the movie to amount to no more than a sympathy for the Spanish Republic and a desire and a willingness to make donations to Spanish Republican causes. Many, many, many people of liberal view shared that outlook. But in the years since 2005, more and more evidence has come to light that, in fact, Oppenheimer was probably a [Communist] party member between 1939 and 1941. That’s the period of the Hitler-Stalin Pact, so this is not a premature anti-fascism. This is not a desire to support the only people who seem to be fighting against Hitler. He joined the party and stayed in it after Stalin signed his pact with Hitler and into the 1941, at least according to the latest suggestive evidence collected post-2005. One of the most eminent historians of the Cold War period and the atomic-research program, Barton Bernstein wrote on the eve of the release of the Oppenheimer movie, “New evidence also leads to a reassessment and thus taking far more seriously, much negative evidence on Oppenheimer dating back to the 1940s that many historians, including myself, often unwisely in about the 1970s to 2002 period, minimized or disregarded. It is no longer possible or reasonable to comfortably conclude, as had many liberal interpreters, including myself, that Oppenheimer in the 1954 hearing”—that’s his security hearing—“was candidly forthcoming about his late 1930s and early 1940s politics. He was not. He lied, and he sought to deceive.” Now, that story about Oppenheimer is relevant to reading this new book about Roy Cohn. Again, in this otherwise encyclopedic and analytic biography of Roy Cohn, you see a minimization of what happened in the 1930s and ’40s with actual Communists. In pages 32 and 33 of American Scoundrel, Kai Bird and Susan Goldmark call Whittaker Chambers a serial fabulist and treat it as an open question whether Alger Hiss was indeed guilty of perjury, and that’s not an open question. We know that not only from the investigations that were taken, conducted at the time, but from later releases of Soviet transcripts that identify Alger Hiss as a Soviet asset in the 1930s. That doesn’t excuse Roy Cohn, who was a scoundrel and who lied and who abused his office and was guilty of, again, things that would get anybody else disbarred or sent to prison. But it does mean that when we reckon with the past, we need to understand that even when we identify the villains correctly, we’re often at risk of identifying the heroes wrongly. Those who are on the wrong side of Roy Cohn were not heroes, even if Roy Cohn was indeed the American scoundrel and great villain that Bird and Goldmark so vividly portray. That’s it for this week’s David Frum Show. Thank you so much for joining me today. I hope if you like the show that you’ll continue subscribing to The Atlantic. That’s the best way to support the work of me and all of my colleagues. Please share this material on any social-media platform you have access to. That helps with the show’s algorithm. See you next week on The David Frum Show. Bye-bye.

items.title: Népal-Tibet : au moins 98 morts dans une crue, des centaines de disparus
items.description: Une crue dévastatrice accompagnée d'un glissement de terrain à la frontière entre le Népal et le Tibet a fait au moins 98 morts mercredi, et plusieurs centaines de personnes sont portées disparues, parmi lesquelles de nombreux touristes étrangers. Les médias d'État chinois ont fait état d'un « lourd bilan humain » après une coulée de boue au niveau d'un important poste-frontière du Tibet, faisant état d'au moins trois morts et 265 personnes portées disparues. Dans une vidéo de surveillance vérifiée par l'AFP, un bâtiment imposant de plusieurs étages ainsi que des personnes qui tentent de fuir sont soudainement engloutis par un torrent très puissant. Une autre, également authentifiée, montre une vague gigantesque, comparable à un tsunami, s'abattre sur un parking en surplomb d'une rivière paisible quelques instants auparavant, balayant autocars et bâtiment avec une force dévastatrice. Le Premier ministre népalais, Balendra Shah, a appelé mercredi la nation himalayenne à « rester unie » et a assuré que « l'Etat est à vos côtés avec tous ses moyens et ressources ». Selon la police népalaise, au moins 95 personnes ont péri alors que les secours continuaient mercredi soir de fouiller la boue et les amas de débris à la recherche de survivants. Dans un décompte provisoire publié sur X, l'Office de tourisme népalais a lui recensé 384 voyageurs manquants, dont 93 sont népalais et 291 sont étrangers. Parmi ces derniers, les nationalités de 111 personnes restent à confirmer, précise l'Office de tourisme. Concernant les autres, 142 personnes sont indiennes et 17 viennent de Malaisie, selon cette source. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères malais a toutefois indiqué que son ambassade à Katmandou avait été informée par les agences de voyage qu'elles avaient perdu le contact avec 11 ressortissants malais dans le district de Rasuwa, frontalier avec la Chine. Par ailleurs, 12 personnes viennent du Royaume-Uni, quatre d'Afrique du Sud, trois des Etats-Unis, une d'Australie et une des Pays-Bas, selon l'Office de tourisme. Des responsables sud-coréens ont pour leur part confirmé que huit de leurs ressortissants qui travaillaient sur une centrale hydroélectrique dans le district de Rasuwa n'avaient pas donné signe de vie après les inondations. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères italien a indiqué de son côté que deux touristes italiens et leur guide s'étaient retrouvés bloqués en amont d'un glissement de terrain mais qu'ils étaient en train d'être secourus. Le ministère a recensé 90 citoyens italiens actuellement au Népal et au Tibet, mais ne sait pas pour l'instant s'ils ont été touchés par la crue. The post Népal-Tibet : au moins 98 morts dans une crue, des centaines de disparus appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Déclassement de la France et taxe Zucman : le patron du Medef appelle à «cesser d’écœurer» les entrepreneurs
items.description: « Fantasmer sur la taxe Zucman et ses avatars ne reglera rien au declassement de la France, bien au contraire », a lance ce 26 août le president du Medef, Patrick Martin, lors de la Rencontre des Entrepreneurs de France – grande-messe patronale qui se tient ces 26 et 27 août – au stade Roland-Garros, a Paris. « Rien, en particulier, sur l'enjeu prioritaire du pouvoir d'achat », a-t-il poursuivi, avant de rappeler que, dans le cas de la France, celui-ci etait desormais inferieur a la moyenne europeenne. « Il faut cesser d'ecœurer ceux qui consacrent leur patrimoine, souvent leur vie, a la prosperite du pays : nous, les entrepreneurs ! », a-t-il ajoute, sous les applaudissements de son public. "Cessez d'écoeurer les entrepreneurs" 👨‍💼 Patrick Martin explique que la taxe Zucman ne permettra pas a la France de sortir du déclassement. Il souligne aussi que les entreprises françaises restent parmi les entreprises les plus taxées au monde. pic.twitter.com/abMowprOTd — BFM Business (@bfmbusiness) August 26, 2026 « Cela veut dire qu'on va remettre en place l'Impot de solidarite sur la fortune, ca veut dire qu'on va mettre en place la taxe Zucman , pour que juste les richesses de ce pays paient autant que le reste du peuple de France », avait declare la veille sur BFMTV et RMC la cheffe des deputes LFI, Mathilde Panot, fustigeant un « systeme ou les riches ont decide de faire secession ». « Veritable » et « seul » probleme : « une depense publique tres excessive » Celle-ci avait egalement evoque la creation de 14 tranches d'imposition pour baisser les impots de ceux qui gagnent moins de 4 000 euros par personne et, sur les heritages, « a partir de 12 millions d'euros nous prendrons tout ». "Les riches ne participent plus à la solidarité nationale, [...] à partir de 12 millions d'euros (d'héritage), nous prendrons tout", déclare Mathilde Panot pic.twitter.com/yK13fi8vza — BFM (@BFMTV) August 25, 2026 Le patron des patrons a egalement appele les parlementaires a « ne pas se laisser impressionner par ce hold-up intellectuel et politique » que constitue a ses yeux la remise en cause du pacte Dutreil, et a eviter de traiter le « veritable, le seul, probleme d'une depense publique tres excessive ». Au-dela du redressement des comptes nationaux pour preserver la souverainete de la France, Patrick Martin a egalement appele a « affronter les contre-verites » du debat public, avant de fustiger le « fantasme dangereux d'annulation de la dette », en reference a l'une des propositions defendues par Jean-Luc Melenchon, candidat a l'election presidentielle de LFI.

items.title: Bobo-Dioulasso : Un Collectif des enseignants mise sur le patrimoine culturel et la réflexion pour restaurer l’image de l’éducateur
items.description: Bobo-Dioulasso : Un Collectif des enseignants mise sur le patrimoine culturel et la réflexion pour restaurer l’image de l’éducateur Bobo-Dioulasso, 26 août 2026 (AIB) – Le Collectif des enseignants du Burkina Faso a organisé, ce mercredi à Bobo-Dioulasso, une visite au mausolée de la Princesse Guimbi Ouattara, suivie d’une conférence publique sur la valorisation du métier d’enseignant. Les deux activités se sont déroulées autour du thème : « Comment l’éducateur peut-il contribuer à restaurer son image ? ». Selon la présidente du Collectif des enseignants du Burkina Faso, Fatimata Lankouandé, le choix du mausolée de la Princesse Guimbi Ouattara pour la visite répond à la volonté de mieux connaître le parcours de cette figure historique, considérée comme un modèle de leadership inspirant. « Nous avons choisi ce cadre parce que, pour nous, la Princesse Guimbi Ouattara est une grande dame au leadership inspirant », a-t-elle expliqué, soulignant la volonté des participants de découvrir davantage son histoire et son parcours. Après cette étape culturelle, les membres du collectif prévoient poursuivre leur programme sur le site de Samandeni Beach, dans une dynamique de détente et de découverte du patrimoine culturel national. Pour le chef des Dioula, Ton massa Moumouni Ouattara, cette initiative constitue une contribution importante à la formation continue des enseignants et à la valorisation de leur profession. Il a salué une activité susceptible de renforcer chez les éducateurs une vision positive de leur métier et de leur rôle dans la société. « Une nation bien éduquée est une nation qui a tous les leviers en main pour le développement », a-t-il déclaré, estimant que l’éducation constitue également un facteur essentiel de cohésion sociale. Le conférencier Sansan Didier Da a expliqué que sa communication a porté sur l’évolution de l’image de l’enseignant, de la période précoloniale à nos jours, en passant par les périodes coloniale et postcoloniale. Il a fait des comparaisons avec la situation des enseignants dans d’autres pays et relevé que la perte de prestige social de la profession est souvent liée aux difficultés économiques et à la baisse du revenu. Sansan Didier Da a insisté sur la responsabilité de l’enseignant lui-même dans la restauration de son image. Il a notamment évoqué la nécessité d’adopter une conduite exemplaire, de renforcer son professionnalisme et de contribuer individuellement à redorer le blason de la profession. Au terme de la conférence, Sansan Didier Da a invité les participants à devenir des « ambassadeurs » auprès de leurs collègues afin de relayer le message et de favoriser, à leur niveau, une amélioration de l’image de l’enseignant dans la société. De son côté, le chef Moumouni Ouattara a jugé le thème particulièrement actuel. Il a relevé que l’enseignant doit construire son autorité autour de trois dimensions : avoir de l’autorité, faire autorité et être l’autorité. Pour lui, la restauration de l’image de l’éducateur relève à la fois de la responsabilité de l’enseignant, de la société et des pouvoirs publics, notamment à travers l’amélioration des conditions d’exercice du métier. Agence d'Information du Burkina OSAR/wis

items.title: Pourquoi le directeur de la CIA s’est-il rendu à Moscou ?
items.description: Le directeur de la CIA, John Ratcliffe, s’est rendu hier, mardi 25 août, à Moscou pour la première fois depuis sa prise de fonction, en janvier 2025. Il s’agit de la visite de plus haut niveau d’un responsable américain en Russie depuis le dernier déplacement de Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, en janvier. La dernière visite connue d’un directeur de la CIA en Russie remonte à novembre 2021, lorsque William Burns, le prédécesseur de Ratcliff, avait mis en garde Poutine contre une tentative d’invasion de l’Ukraine. Le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, avait déclaré mardi 25 lors d’une conférence de presse ne « disposer d'aucune information » concernant l'arrivée à Moscou d’un avion de transport de l’armée américaine, dont le vol depuis Riga avait été repéré quelques heures plus tôt par des analystes OSINT. Aujourd’hui, mercredi 26, Peskov a déclaré que Poutine n’avait pas rencontré Ratcliffe lors de sa visite, et que les seuls contacts entre celui-ci et le Kremlin avaient eu lieu « par l'intermédiaire des services de renseignement » russes Песков : контактов Путина и директора ЦРУ Рэтклиффа не было », TASS , 26 août 2026.'> 1 . Le flou entourant les motifs de la visite de Ratcliffe à Moscou, alors que l’attention de l’administration Trump est principalement tournée vers l’Iran depuis février, alimente les spéculations. Plusieurs chaînes Telegram russes évoquent des négociations relatives à la libération d’un prisonnier américain, Charles Wayne Zimmerman, arrêté en 2025 puis condamné en janvier à cinq ans de prison pour être entré en Russie avec une arme Publication sur Telegram de Кровавая барыня , 25 août 2026.'> 2 . Un vol américain avec un itinéraire similaire avait eu lieu l’an dernier pour libérer l’enseignant américain Mark Fogel, condamné en 2022 à 14 ans de prison pour trafic de cannabis, en échange de l’homme d’affaires russe Alexander Vinnik. Une autre hypothèse, avancée par des analystes cités par le Wall Street Journal , évoque une visite destinée à mettre en garde Poutine contre toute velléité de « tester la détermination de l’OTAN » par des attaques contre l’Alliance CIA Director John Ratcliffe Makes Surprise Trip to Moscow », The Wall Street Journal , 25 août 2026.'> 3 . Les renseignements américains estiment que la Russie pourrait chercher à escalader sa guerre hybride menée contre l’Europe en lançant des cyberattaques, voire en envoyant des combattants dans un pays du flanc Est de l’Alliance. Les opérations de sabotage russes en Europe ont presque quadruplé entre 2023 et 2024. La Russie a fréquemment recours à des agents « jetables » pour mener des opérations de sabotage, d’espionnage, de diversion ou d’autres attaques hors de son territoire national. D'autres sources évoquent de possibles discussions visant à associer la Russie aux négociations avec l'Iran. Moscou soutient activement le régime de Téhéran en lui livrant, via la mer Caspienne, des composants destinés à la fabrication de drones, de munitions et d'explosifs. La visite a été en partie coordonnée avec l'Ukraine, à qui les États-Unis ont demandé de « suspendre les frappes » sur Moscou et sa région jusqu'au départ de Ratcliffe CIA director Ratcliffe visits Moscow », Axios , 25 août 2026.'> 4 . Donald Trump, qui a confirmé mercredi 26 la visite, a suggéré qu'elle pourrait servir les efforts pour mettre fin à la guerre en Ukraine, déclarant : « Il pourrait en ressortir quelque chose. Nous travaillons d'arrache-pied pour que cette guerre prenne fin ». Une visite à Moscou de Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, principaux négociateurs de Trump, initialement prévue avant la fin du mois d'août, a été reportée la semaine dernière. Ces derniers auraient également « repoussé » une visite prévue à Kiev « en raison des frappes de missiles et de drones ». L’article Pourquoi le directeur de la CIA s’est-il rendu à Moscou ? est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: WFP warns global conflict is driving Sudan deeper into hunger crisis
items.description: The World Food Programme (WFP) has warned that global conflict and disruptions to fuel and trade are worsening Sudan’s already catastrophic hunger crisis, with basic food costs rising by almost 40 per cent since February. Addressing the UN Security Council on Monday, WFP Acting Executive Director Carl Skau described Sudan as the world’s worst hunger crisis and warned that conflict far beyond its borders was also driving up food prices for Sudanese families. “One oil tanker anchored in the Strait of Hormuz can mean one less meal a day for a child in Sudan,” Skau said. “Conflict is the leading driver of hunger around the world,” he added. “It is not only a consequence of conflict , it is increasingly being used as a weapon.” ‘Look at Sudan’ Skau urged the international community to act before famine is officially declared , saying earlier intervention could have prevented further suffering in Sudan. “Take action before famine is declared and before agricultural seasons are lost. Just look at Sudan,” he told the Council. “With decisive early action, we may have prevented famine last year in the world’s worst hunger crisis.” He also criticised the international response to warnings ahead of atrocities in El Fasher . “We all saw the atrocities in El-Fasher coming, but the international community, including this council, failed to act on those warnings,” Skau said. Recalling a visit to Tawila in Darfur, where survivors of El Fasher have sought refuge, he described “700,000 people in a super city of grass huts” who had arrived with nothing and now depended on limited humanitarian aid . “The people I met there felt completely abandoned,” he said. Skau stressed that waiting for famine to be declared was “a total failure of duty” and called for stronger protection of civilians, food systems and humanitarian access. “We can’t pull back in Sudan just as we secure access for scaling up,” he said, urging urgent political action alongside humanitarian assistance. items.title: Situationer: Unanswered questions linger hours after Pims fire tragedy
items.description: At around 4:30 pm, almost 10 hours after the fire that killed 14 infants, the entrance to the gynaecology ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Science (Pims) remained crowded. Eyewitnesses and relatives of victims had been hushed away hours ago, and the families left when the bodies were handed over. But there was an army of reporters and a line of cameramen set up in a neat row, waiting to see if anyone would show up. Everyone felt there was more to the story. The Mother Children Hospital (MCH) ward, situated at the western end of the healthcare facility, was sealed soon after the fire was reported. The main entrance at the north was also cordoned off with yellow tape, which has since been knocked down by the rush of people. To ensure the ward remained sealed, several policemen were posted at the gate, in addition to the hospital guards inside, apparently to ensure no daredevil reporter or cameraman was able to get inside. A bag of riot control gear, batons included, lay outside the entrance. For some strange reason, officials from the Punjab Highway Police prowled around the scene. Reporters and cameraman at the PIMS hospital in Islamabad hours after a fire killed 14 infants at the facility. — All photos by author A woman carrying a sick child was arguing with the policemen at the gate when I arrived. She held up the child and pleaded for several minutes until the guard inside finally relented and opened the gate just enough to let her in. As if on cue, a few reporters darted forward, but the door was swung shut again before they could get to it. Soon after, the reporters turned their attention towards a different source of commotion: a man started screaming and cameras gathered around. People in the crowd asked him if he had lost a child, but the man ignored the question. He simply exhorted the reporters that God would not forgive them if they didn’t go inside and report the truth of the matter. “They are martyrs,” he screamed before walking away. Rumours, denials The chatter was the same everywhere. Conflicting timelines, locked doors and whispers of coverups. Several people asked where exactly the nursery ward was located; most reporters and onlookers had never been inside the hospital. There was a general sense that no one truly knew what had happened. One person on the site confidently told me that the fire began due to a fault in the air conditioning system. Another said he knew for a fact there was a fault in the incubators. Rescue teams broke into the building by punching holes into the concrete grill and climbing though the window. — All images by author The only sign that a rescue operation had taken place here were some broken windows; a few by people before the rescue teams arrived. They said the bulk of the rescue was done by the people themselves. The fire brigade team that carried out the initial rescue had rotated out of their shift by 2pm. The new team sat on the ground next to a parked fire truck, even though the fire had long been extinguished. A member of the replacement team showed me the two places the building had been broken into. Firefighters had reached the site to find both the northern and western gates locked, he told me. Several people on the scene told me that locking the maternity ward was usual business; there is a fear of newborns being kidnapped. So the firefighters had set up ladders, broken two big holes into the building and carried out the initial rescue. Some said the fire brigade team only carried out adults stuck in the ward. The replacement firemen weren’t sure themselves. Journalist Qurrat-ul-AIn Shirazi showed me a video of a fireman bringing down a small wrapped body. “Everyone gives a different timeline, a different version,” she told me. Alina Shahid, a journalist, also told me that the rescue operation was wrapped up before 11am and the bodies handed over to the families. She also said eyewitnesses told her that the initial rescue operations were impeded. The bodies were moved to a mortuary, quickly identified and handed over soon after the operation ended. “They [families] were handed the bodies and hurried away from the scene,” a woman on the scene told me. “Everything seemed to be happening in a hurry.” Farah Rabbani, a journalist who had arrived at the site just after 9am, told me that she truly realised things were serious when she received a video from the Edhi rescue service showing small coffins being prepared. She was perhaps one of the few reporters who actually managed to get inside the ward. “It’s completely destroyed,” she told me, “floor to ceiling, everything is burnt.” The other entrance that had also been sealed is at the western end. There were no reporters gathered there so I decided to see for myself. A moment later, I realised why. That side of the building has an open corridor blocked only by a grill. And through that grill came what can only be described as the worst smell I have ever experienced: burnt plastic and charred flesh. The western entrance, which opens into a corridor, was deserted. All photos by author Questions remain Politicians came and went. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal had left minutes before I arrived. PPP’s Sherry Rehman had visited before him. Soon, leader of the opposition in the Senate, Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, appeared and took care to emphasise that not letting the media in was an attempt at a cover up. Minutes after he left, PPP’s Shahid Khattak was on the scene. The lines were repetitive; the questions remained. Had the bodies been identified? This was another question that elicited several confident responses. Some said the tags placed on the infants’ limbs were intact. Others said identification was still in process. None of the people who could actually answer the questions were on the scene anymore.

items.title: Team unable to locate Pakistani climber Asma Mushtaq's body on Spantik after hours-long efforts
items.description: A recovery team has descended back to Camp 2 from the spot on Gilgit-Baltistan’s Spantik Peak where the body of deceased Pakistani climber Asma Mushtaq was suspected to be buried under the snow, an official said. The 34-year-old climber died on Aug 20 while descending from the mountain, also known as Golden Peak, after suffering from high-altitude sickness. Her body was said to be at Camp 3, which is located at a height of approximately 6,250 metres. Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that the six-member team reached Camp 3 on Wednesday, where the body was suspected to be. However, he added, the team could not find the body after several hours of intense search. He said it was unclear whether the team would continue their search on Thursday or delay the mission, stressing the weather’s importance. Shigri said it was feared that the climber’s body was buried under snow after the peak received fresh snowfall, adding that there were also high winds at the peak. Highlighting that the six-member local team consists of highly professional climbers, Shigri said Pakistan Army helicopters were expected to airlift Mushtaq’s body to Skardu after its arrival at the base camp. The ACP member pointed out that helicopters could not retrieve the body from altitudes over 6,000m. “Only the ground rescue team can bring down the body from the peak to base camp,” he emphasised. In a post on social media earlier, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar also noted that as the “place is very large and due to heavy snowfall over the past two days, the body is now completely covered under the snow, making it difficult to locate”. According to the minister, the rescue team’s search efforts had been ongoing for two hours as of around 4pm. The team had resumed its search operation on Tuesday once weather conditions improved, after heavy snowfall had halted the retrieval efforts on Sunday. During her ascent, Mushtaq had successfully reached the 7,027-metre summit of Spantik and was in good health at the time, the ACP said in statements issued on Thursday. However, she developed a serious high-altitude medical emergency at an elevation of about 6,400 metres during the descent. High-altitude sickness encompasses a range of pulmonary and cerebral conditions caused by hypoxia, or oxygen deprivation, due to rapid ascent and inadequate acclimatisation to high altitudes. Shigri earlier told Dawn that Mushtaq was part of a five-member Pakistani women’s expedition team that summited Spantik, which included climbers Zoni Aslam, Zaba Shigri, Shama and Sohana. Climate change-induced shifts in weather patterns have worsened conditions on the peaks of the Karakoram Range in GB, creating serious difficulties for mountaineers. Body of US climber shifted to Islamabad Meanwhile, the body of US climber Sarah Mallory Geis was shifted to Islamabad on Wednesday for repatriation to her country, a day after it was airlifted to Skardu. ACP’s Shigri told Dawn that the body was dispatched via Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) from Skardu Airport on Wednesday morning. The body was received by an international insurance company that is responsible for its repatriation to her country. Geis was among the 10 mountaineers who lost their lives after being struck by an avalanche on Broad Peak (8,047 metres) last month. Her body was recovered from Broad Peak 22 days after she went missing in the deadly incident. Up until now, Geis was one of the last two climbers from the expedition whose bodies could not be retrieved. Earlier, Shigri said that the search for the last member of the expedition, Nawang Thindu Sherpa, was also under way.

items.title: Houet : le Maouloud célébré sous le signe de la paix et de la cohésion sociale à Péni
items.description: Houet : le Maouloud célébré sous le signe de la paix et de la cohésion sociale à Péni Péni, 26 août 2026 (AIB) – La communauté musulmane de la commune de Péni a célébré, dans la nuit du 25 au 26 août 2026, le Maouloud, commémorant la naissance du prophète Mohamed, sous le signe de la paix, de la solidarité et de la cohésion sociale. La cérémonie a réuni des fidèles musulmans ainsi que des représentants des autorités administratives, militaires et paramilitaires, de la chefferie coutumière et des invités venus d’autres localités. Le préfet, président de la Délégation spéciale de la commune de Péni, Moumouni Ouédraogo, a félicité la communauté musulmane pour l’organisation de la célébration. Il a salué son accompagnement des initiatives de la délégation spéciale et appelé les populations à renforcer la solidarité, la cohésion sociale et le vivre-ensemble, tout en les invitant à se démarquer de toute forme de manipulation. Au nom de la chefferie coutumière, le représentant le chef du village de Péni, Yacouba Ouattara, a salué les organisateurs et formulé des vœux de paix et de cohésion sociale. Le prêche a été animé par le président de la communauté musulmane, Adama Dao. Il a évoqué le contexte de la naissance du prophète Mohamed et rappelé l’importance du Maouloud pour les fidèles musulmans. Il a également exhorté les populations à promouvoir la solidarité, la paix et le vivre-ensemble, avant de conclure par des prières et des bénédictions en faveur de la commune de Péni. La célébration a enregistré la participation de fidèles venus d’autres localités, témoignant de la dimension spirituelle et sociale de cette commémoration. Agence d'Information du Burkina MO/AB/wis

items.title: Lélouma : des tables bancs de la fac à la production de la banane, le pari osé d’un jeune diplômé
items.description: Après plusieurs années d'études, Mamadou Oury Diallo aurait pu chercher un emploi dans un bureau ou bien tenter sa chance ailleurs. Mais il a préféré jeter son dévolu sur l'agriculture. Aujourd'hui, il se consacre à la production de la banane. Avec trois de ses amis, il se lance dans un pari des plus audacieux. Voilà, les quatre amis qui engagent leurs économies et leurs énergies pour réaliser une plantation de trois hectares avec plus de 15 mille pieds de bananes. Un choix très osé. Une autre manière de voir l'agriculture, au-delà de la tradition. » Après plusieurs années d'études par-ci, par-là, j'ai décidé de rentrer chez nous ici, lancer cette plantation avec trois de mes amis sur les rives de Komba dans la sous-préfecture de Lafou. (…). Et ce que vous voyez là, c'est le fruit d'un travail d'une année. Et le résultat est vraiment prometteur », se réjouit, dès l'entame, le jeune homme. Sur trois hectares, 15 mille pieds de bananes se développent à une incroyable vitesse. » Ça fait presque une année depuis que nous avons lancé cette activité. (…). Tout se passe pour le moment très bien. (…). Au lieu de se lancer à l'aventure avec tous les risques, nous avons préféré retourner la terre et pourquoi pas essayer de réussir ici chez nous, avec, à la clé, cette agriculture. En tout cas, nous y croyons et avec la volonté de Dieu, nous allons y arriver. Ça n'a pas été facile mais ça commence, peu à peu, à prendre forme ». Cependant, le problème lié à l'accès à la plantation et à celui du marché constitue un véritable handicap pour ce quatuor de jeunes. Pourtant, le groupe ne compte pas s'arrêter là. Il a déjà acquis un autre domaine d'environ cinq hectares qu'il entend mettre très vite en valeur. Les cultures vivrières aussi, sont en perspective. Pour mener à bien ce projet, ces jeunes sollicitent des appuis et un accompagnement auprès des bailleurs, ONG et autres institutions, pour relever le défi lié au développement de la localité.
